properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Well-known public Hardhat/Anvil development-account keys (0xac0974bec… is Hardhat account #0, 0x5de4111a… account #19; 0x28b2b031… is the zkevm local test-chain key) used by pool and e2e tests to fund throwaway local chains. They control no production funds, but they are real secp256k1 key material committed as literals and would be CWE-321 material if the same pattern reached a real deployment. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum's transaction signature scheme is ECDSA over secp256k1. These sites are test-key generation and API-schema documentation; the production uses are the fakevm ecrecover precompile (crypto.Ecrecover, contracts.go:186) and L1 tx signing via go-ethereum's bind signer (etherman.go:1996), reported as separate findings. Shor-broken, but the scheme is protocol-bound to the EVM/ecosystem — migrating it (e.g. to ML-DSA via account abstraction) is an ecosystem decision, not a repo-local change.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto v0.28.0 is a DIRECT dependency and its sha3 sub-package provides SHAKE128 alongside Keccak. No first-party SHAKE/XOF call site exists (repo-wide grep finds no NewShake/NewXOF); the primitive ships in the build and is reachable by any future code. Presence is the inventory question; use is not.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same provider as the SHAKE128 entry: golang.org/x/crypto v0.28.0 sha3 sub-package provides SHAKE256. No first-party call site found; available in the shipped library. SHAKE256 (512-bit output) is the CNSA 2.0-recommended XOF baseline.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWT (typically HS256/HMAC-SHA256) is quantum-relevant mainly as a MAC with a harvestable shared secret. Here the library is only transitively present (go.mod marks it // indirect); no engine-API-style JWT endpoint is implemented in this node. If a future feature signs JWTs, the HS256 default is the weak spot (HMAC secret + quantum search); RS256/ES256 key material would be Shor-relevant instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go's crypto/rand (OS entropy via getrandom/ChaCha20). Used to generate random test fixtures in pool and sequencer tests. The production path for key randomness is go-ethereum's crypto.GenerateKey (also crypto/rand-backed), called at etherman.go:2013 for throwaway gas-estimation keys. Not quantum-relevant; a healthy PRNG posture.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ProtonMail's OpenPGP implementation (RSA/EdDSA signing, AES/Salsa20 session ciphers, iterated KDFs) shipped in the build via go-git v5, which the node's test/dependency tooling uses for git operations (commit/tag signature verification). No first-party OpenPGP call site. The algorithms are classical and Shor/Grover-weakened respectively, but exposure is limited to whatever go-git verifies.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Cloudflare's crypto library ships classical primitives (X25519, Ed25519, P-256, ChaCha20-Poly1305) plus early-PQ experiments; indirect via go-git v5. No first-party circl call site, but the algorithms are compiled into the shipped module graph. Observable here; replaceable only by changing go-git's dependency chain.
